prompt:
Deliverable and intended use:
Create exactly one 1536 x 1024 landscape decorative artwork for the quiet personal-life interlude of a sophisticated dark nautical portfolio website. The artwork is an imagined cinematic miniature scene, not an actual personal travel photograph. It must have no text, no typography, no people, no UI and no logos.

Reference role:
Image 1 is a material, atmosphere and color reference only. Preserve its finely crafted physically rendered miniature aesthetic, tactile aged wood and warm metal, calm night ocean, moonlit dark teal palette and restrained warm practical lights. Change only the depicted scene and composition into the coastal road and quiet camping viewpoint specified below; preserve the reference's material language and dark nautical mood. Do not retain the pirate ship, circular table, navigation interface, portrait, journal, compass or any writing from the reference.

Scene and subjects:
A gently curving coastal mountain road enters from the lower right, passes a small seaside stopping place at middle right, then traces a soft arc toward a distant modest lighthouse on an atmospheric headland. A single small vintage forest-green travel station wagon is parked beside the road at the viewpoint, pointing loosely toward the distant lighthouse. It is unbranded with realistic proportions, blank dark plates, classic round lamps and softly weathered painted metal. A single fishing rod rests at a diagonal against a rough wooden coastal post nearby. On the ground near the car, one small canvas travel bag and a warmly glowing old camping lantern form a quiet lived-in detail. The rod, bag and lamp are secondary and physically plausible, not arranged as a product display. A tiny pale sailboat far offshore completes the view. No other vehicles or objects. Keep the scene simple, poetic and comfortable.

Composition and camera:
Low three-quarter cinematic view with a subtle handcrafted miniature scale, not an isometric icon or top-down map. The foreground car and warm campsite occupy the right half, between x=920 and x=1380 and y=470 and y=840. The road draws the eye from bottom right toward the distant headland and lighthouse around x=1170, y=360. The entire left 43 percent of the frame is uninterrupted very dark low-contrast teal ocean, mist and spacious sky, calm enough for website copy. The open sea spreads leftward, creating visual breathing room. Horizon around upper 40 percent. Keep the main car fully visible with breathing room. The landscape is continuous across the full image without a visible diorama base, plinth, border or cutout edge. The road is a narrow secondary visual curve, not a bright highway. Natural quiet composition, no crowded foreground arrangement.

Light, color and material:
Deep blue-hour evening nearing night, with muted twilight in distant clouds and only a restrained lighthouse glow. Dark ocean #061a22, muted deep teal water, slate coastal rocks, soft forest greens, pale desaturated sky reflection, warm antique-copper and amber lantern illumination. The lantern spills a small warm pool onto the gravel, car door and bag; the atmosphere feels human and peaceful despite no person being shown. Premium physically rendered 3D miniature with lifelike wet rock, brushed weathered car paint, rough wood, canvas and gentle ocean ripples. Distant coastal forms soften naturally with atmospheric perspective. Use visual depth, delicate edge highlights and rich shadows. Keep the highlights subdued enough to sit within a dark website. Lower and left edges gently settle toward #061a22 for seamless blending, without an obvious vignette frame.

Invariants and exclusions:
One car, one fishing rod, one lantern, one travel bag, one distant lighthouse and one tiny sailboat. No people or animals. No pirates or pirate symbols. No neon or sci-fi glow, no laser beams, no giant moon, no sparkles, no decorative particles, no floating items, no surreal road geometry, no extra camping clutter, no plastic cartoon look. No interface, no labels, no title, no caption, no signature, no watermark, no branding, no legible license plate, no letters or numbers anywhere. This is a single cohesive decorative coastal artwork, not a webpage mockup and not a collage.
